title: Counters: three simple rules
summary: Counters are nouns that act like adverbs. You need only about a dozen, you can often use ひとつ、ふたつ instead, and sound changes only affect certain kana.

blocks.text: To count things Japanese puts a **counter** between the number and the thing: 犬 is counted 一匹, a bird 一羽, a sheet 一枚. There are dozens, but only about a dozen are common, and you can pick them up as you go. When you read or hear a number followed by a little word, you already know that little word is a counter.
Rule 1: most of the time you can avoid them
The **native counting** ひとつ、ふたつ、みっつ... (一つ、二つ、三つ) needs no counter and works for nearly everything except people and small animals.

blocks.jp: りんごを三つください。

blocks.text: Rule 2: counters are nouns, used in two ways

Counters are **nouns**, so they take の before another noun, just like any noun. But they are also special nouns that can modify a **verb** like an adverb. 猫が三匹いる is literally "cats exist in a three-small-animal way", which is why the sentence ends in a verb.

blocks.en: Three cats are in the garden. (counter + の + noun)
There are three cats. (the counter describes the verb)

blocks.text: Rule 3: sound changes follow a pattern

A counter whose first kana **cannot take a dakuten** (the ten-ten) never changes: 枚 (ま), 輪 (り) stay the same after any number. Changes only happen in kana rows that can take dakuten or a small っ, such as 匹 (ひき: いっぴき, さんびき) and 本. Learn them as you meet them.

items: About a dozen common counters: 枚 (flat), 本 (long), 冊 (books), 匹 (small animals), 羽 (birds), 人 (people).
Native counting (一つ、二つ) avoids counters for most objects.
Counters are nouns that can also work like adverbs: 猫が三匹いる.
If the counter's first kana can't take a ten-ten, its sound never changes.

questions.note: 匹 counts small animals.
枚 counts flat things.

questions.en: There are four birds in the tree.
questions.note: 羽 counts birds.
冊 counts books.
本 counts long, thin things.

questions.note: 一つ、二つ... needs no counter for most objects.

questions.instruction: Which cannot be counted with the native counting (ひとつ、ふたつ)?
questions.note: People and small animals have their own counters.
Native counting 三つ works for cakes.

questions.instruction: Which counter fits flat things such as paper?
questions.note: 枚 is for flat things.

questions.instruction: Which counter fits long things such as bottles?
questions.note: 本 is for long, thin things.
冊 is for bound books.

questions.instruction: Why does a sentence like 犬が二匹いる end in a verb?
options: The counter describes the verb like an adverb
questions.note: The counter works as an adverb: "dogs exist in a two-animal way".

questions.instruction: Why do counters take の before another noun?
questions.note: Counters are nouns, so they take の like any noun.

questions.instruction: Why does 枚 never change its sound?
options: Its first kana ま cannot take a ten-ten or small っ
questions.note: Sound changes happen only in rows that can take dakuten or small っ.

questions.instruction: Which counter's first kana can take a ten-ten, so its sound can change?
questions.note: ひ can become び or ぴ: さんびき.

questions.instruction: How do you say 一匹?
questions.note: The sound changes after 一.

questions.instruction: How do you say 三匹?
questions.note: After ん the sound becomes び.
二匹 is a number plus the counter 匹.

questions.instruction: Tap the counter that comes before の
questions.note: Counter + の + noun.
The counter works like an adverb before the verb.
